1. Clark requires every belief in a subject’s chain of grounds to be true.
2. Smith implicitly relies on the belief that Jones’s owning a Ford yesterday would result in Jones’s owning a Ford now.
3. The implicit linking belief is false in the Saunders–Champawat case.
4. If Clark requires every ground to be true and Smith has a false linking ground, then Clark’s analysis says that Smith does not know that Jones owns a Ford now.
5. Clark is an analyst of knowledge.
6. If X is an analyst of knowledge and X requires every belief in a subject’s chain of grounds to be true, then X requires every ground to be true.
7. Therefore, Clark requires every ground to be true. [1,5,6]
8. Smith is a subject of a knowledge claim.
9. If X is a subject of a knowledge claim and X implicitly relies on the belief that Jones’s owning a Ford yesterday would result in Jones’s owning a Ford now and the implicit linking belief is false in the Saunders–Champawat case, then X has a false linking ground.
10. Therefore, Smith has a false linking ground. [2,3,8,9]
11. Therefore, Clark’s analysis says that Smith does not know that Jones owns a Ford now. [4,7,10]
12. Clark’s analysis denies knowledge on account of Smith’s false linking ground.
13. Clark’s analysis is a theory of knowledge.
14. If X is a theory of knowledge and X denies knowledge on account of Smith’s false linking ground, then supplementing the description with that ground blocks the putative counterexample to X.
15. Therefore, supplementing the description with that ground blocks the putative counterexample to Clark’s analysis. [12,13,14]
16. The putative counterexample to Clark’s analysis is identical to the Saunders–Champawat putative counterexample to Clark.
17. The putative counterexample to Clark’s analysis is an objection to a theory of knowledge.
18. If X is an objection to a theory of knowledge and X is identical to Y and supplementing the description with that ground blocks X, then Y is blocked by supplementing the description with that ground.
19. Therefore, the Saunders–Champawat putative counterexample to Clark is blocked by supplementing the description with that ground. [15,16,17,18]
20. Therefore, (Clark’s analysis says that Smith does not know that Jones owns a Ford now) and (the Saunders–Champawat putative counterexample to Clark is blocked by supplementing the description with that ground). [11,19]
